name: deja
tagline: Predictive inline shell autosuggestions for zsh
description: deja is a smarter replacement for zsh-autosuggestions that predicts the command you actually want to run — as inline ghost text after every keystroke, with zero latency. Instead of only surfacing commands that start with what you typed, it combines fuzzy matching, directory awareness, and command-sequence prediction, so it knows you usually run make test after make build and that commands from your current project rank higher. A lightweight Go daemon serves every terminal window over a Unix socket with sub-millisecond responses, and all data stays in a local SQLite database. Ghost text renders through zsh's region_highlight, an alternatives picker cycles ranked candidates with Tab, and three fuzzy presets tune how strictly typed letters must cluster. Privacy is a first-class concern: deja honors HIST_IGNORE_SPACE and HISTORY_IGNORE, so secret-laden commands are never recorded.
highlights: Predicts next commands with fuzzy matching, directory affinity, and sequence scoring
Go daemon serves all terminals over a Unix socket, sub-millisecond per keystroke
Ghost text inline via zsh region_highlight, with Tab alternatives picker
Frecency scoring blends frequency and recency with a one-week exponential decay
Local-only SQLite storage that honors zsh history ignore rules for privacy
curatorNote: Most autosuggestions complete what you started typing; deja predicts what you would type next, and it weighs where you are and what you just ran. A genuinely thoughtful take on the zsh-autosuggestions formula, surfaced on r/commandline while still small.
